what: The machine-readable half of the P1-28 closing package. It names ONE commit as the phase's code candidate and records every measurement taken against it, with the provenance of each. docs/phase-1/phase-1-28/evidence/closure-evidence.md is the prose half and must state the same candidate; scripts/ci/build-p1-28-evidence-manifest.mjs refuses a disagreement between the two.
why: P1-27 shipped a closing page that pinned a head 47 commits behind the tree it described, and it went on reading like evidence because nothing compared the claim with the repository. A closing value that names no head is not a measurement of anything. Every figure below therefore carries the head it was taken at and the artefact it came from.
whatThisIsNot: This is not a tamper-proof seal and not a hosted observation. The digests in evidence-manifest.json remove SILENT revision, not revision. NO HOSTED FIGURE IN THIS PACKAGE WAS TAKEN AT THIS CANDIDATE, and re-freezing the candidate did not change that. Every one of them comes from run 31750364479, which measured 38afa5c28e5b78d484a442cf6b8596fb2a5c34aa — a head three fix waves have since superseded — and each is recorded PENDING here, marked `describesSupersededHead`, and listed in `pendingHostedBindings`. What a later reader can do with them is fetch the same objects and see what that head did; what nobody may do with them is read them as a measurement of this candidate.

candidate.subject: fix(ci): resolve a citation with one read, not a check then a use
candidate.whatFreezingMeans: Every LOCAL figure in this package describes THIS commit. Commits that land after it are DOCUMENTATION-ONLY: each is required to leave apps/** and supabase/** byte-identical, and the successor list is empty because nothing executable follows this candidate. A successor that changes a product tree invalidates this package and the candidate must be re-frozen and re-measured, which is recorded in `reFrozenFrom` below for every candidate this package has named.

reFrozenFrom.what: Every candidate this package has named, most recent first. Kept rather than overwritten: deleting the record of what was once frozen is the half-update this gate exists to catch.

history.whyItMoved: A CodeQL HIGH landed against the citation resolver this package commissioned: `js/file-system-race` at `scripts/ci/check-p1-28-traceability.mjs`, where `existsSync` then `statSync` then `readFileSync` asked whether a path was a readable file and then read it — and the answer a sealed record quotes could have changed between the question and the read. `3c75f49a01e35b507461bf0929b0046e7140860a` resolves it with ONE `readFileSync`, carrying the distinction in the FAILURE instead (`ENOENT` -> names no file at this head, `EISDIR` -> names a directory, not a file, anything else rethrown), and drops `statSync` from the import. The return strings are unchanged, so the gate still derives 27 claims across 8 documents with 0 disagreements.
history.whyReFrozenRatherThanNamed: Both were open and the choice was deliberate. `git diff --name-only b5e9919b..3c75f49a -- apps supabase` is EMPTY and the only executable path that differs is `scripts/ci/check-p1-28-traceability.mjs`, so this commit COULD have been named an executable successor with that path declared as `measurementDrift`. Naming it was rejected for three reasons. First, the drift apparatus exists for the case where a re-freeze is IMPOSSIBLE because a product path moved; using it when the front door is open weakens what it means when it is used. Second, the invariant that the candidate IS the newest commit touching an executable path is the strongest true statement this package can make, and it is what ended the reseal treadmill — naming would re-open that accumulation one commit at a time and pose the same fork at every future repair. Third, nothing is lost: what this commit did and why is recorded here with the fidelity a successor entry would have carried. Neither choice made any known-bad world vacuous; that was checked before choosing, and is not why the choice was made.
history.whatThisCostAndWhatItDidNot: It cost the two local tiers, re-measured here at the new candidate. It bought no hosted figure: every hosted binding remains PENDING and every superseded-head citation for 38afa5c2 stands exactly as it stood.
history.supersededSuccessorRecord: That candidate named no executable successor at the moment it was superseded; `3c75f49a01e35b507461bf0929b0046e7140860a` is now the candidate itself.

history.whyItMoved: Part of the same deliberate re-freeze as the entry below, and separated from it only because a package cannot be made true at a head without landing the commit that makes it true. Freezing at `34b3fca5` turned one tree-level falsification VACUOUS — the case cleared `successors` on the current candidate and required the unnamed executable commits to be reported, which a candidate that IS the newest executable commit cannot have — and its own anti-vacuity guard reported that rather than passing on an empty set. Re-anchoring that case on a SUPERSEDED candidate, where executable history exists by definition, is itself an executable change, so it became the candidate. `git diff --name-only 34b3fca5..b5e9919b -- apps supabase` is EMPTY; nothing but the seal own test moved.

candidate.vocabularyNote: `FINAL_CODE_SHA` and `FINAL_CODE_TREE` are the names this package was commissioned under and are used here so the commissioning brief and this record cannot drift apart. They are NOT the P1-27 spelling: that phase says `CODE_CANDIDATE_SHA` for the same idea, and no file in this repository used `FINAL_CODE_*` before this one. The mapping is recorded below rather than left for a reader to guess, because two names for one commit is exactly how a superseded head gets quoted as a current one.

vocabularyMapping.FINAL_CODE_SHA: P1-27 calls this CODE_CANDIDATE_SHA — the newest commit touching any non-document path.
vocabularyMapping.FINAL_CODE_TREE: The tree object of that commit. P1-27 records no equivalent field; it is added here because a tree id is what makes two checkouts comparable without trusting a commit message.
vocabularyMapping.EVIDENCE_RECORD_SHA: P1-27's name for the commit carrying the evidence file — here, the documentation-only commit that carries this record, which the gate PRINTS rather than requires to be named because a commit cannot name itself.
vocabularyMapping.EXECUTABLE_DIFF_COUNT: P1-27's derivation `git diff --name-only CODE_CANDIDATE_SHA..EVIDENCE_RECORD_SHA` excluding docs/ and *.md. DOCUMENTATION_ONLY_RECORDING may be claimed only when it is exactly zero. Since the re-freeze it IS zero for every commit after this candidate — the candidate is the newest commit touching an executable path and `successors` is empty — so this package now satisfies the P1-27 rule outright. Earlier revisions did not and said so: they named executable machinery successors and claimed the narrower checkable thing instead, that apps/** and supabase/** were byte-identical.

successorRule.what: EMPTY, and that is the point of the re-freeze. The candidate IS the newest commit touching an executable path, so nothing executable follows it and there is nothing to name. Commits after it carry this record and are DOCUMENTATION-ONLY; the gate PRINTS them rather than demanding they be named, because a commit cannot write its own id into a file it contains.
successorRule.whatWouldFailThis: Any commit after the candidate that touches a path outside `docs/` which is not `*.md`. The gate computes the range with `git log <head under test> --not <candidate> <base>` and refuses an unnamed executable one, so re-freezing does not disarm the rule - it empties the list the rule reads.

howTierFiguresAreChecked: Four obligations, because there are four kinds of claim. ARITHMETIC: `passed + failed + skipped` must equal the declared total, for every tier — the review set `passed: 3, failed: 812` beside `tests: 2475` and the first revision of the gate accepted it, because nothing added the three numbers up. LOCAL: the figures must equal the P1-27 run ledger’s, read out of git at the commit named in `localLedger.atCommit`, and a LOCAL tier may carry no figure the ledger does not write. MEASUREMENT HEAD: the head a local tier names must be executable-identical to the candidate, or a NAMED successor of it carrying no product drift and declaring `measurementDrift` exactly equal to what `git diff --name-only <head>..<candidate>` computes. Both local tiers now name the candidate ITSELF, so the first branch applies and neither declares drift. HOSTED: cannot be computed from this repository at all, and the gate says so in those words; what it requires instead is that the claim be FETCHABLE — a run id, a job id, the head the job ran at, and the artefact — and, when that head is not the candidate, that the record SAY WHICH OF TWO THINGS IT IS — a head the candidate SUPERSEDES, marked `describesSupersededHead`, proved an ancestor and listed in `pendingHostedBindings`; or a head that DESCENDS from the candidate, marked `describesProductIdenticalSuccessor`, whose apps/** and supabase/** `git diff` computes to be identical to the candidate's. Either way the head must be a commit this repository contains.

ownerAcceptance.rule: The permanent Frontend closure rule from P1-26 onward: no Frontend phase closes without the Product Owner testing the running application in real installed Chrome and returning `OWNER ACCEPTANCE: PASS` verbatim. Silence is never Pass. Automated CI is necessary and is not sufficient.
ownerAcceptance.howToRun: npm run acceptance:serve — a production build, never dev:all. A dev stack compiles route bundles lazily and the API authenticator is installed as a side effect of composing the IAM module, so an acceptance session on a dev stack reports product defects that do not exist.
ownerAcceptance.note: This package is the technical evidence an acceptance session rests on. It is NOT a closure record and does not close the phase. IT IS ALSO NOT YET THE COMPLETE TECHNICAL EVIDENCE: eleven hosted bindings are PENDING at this candidate (see `pendingHostedBindings`). An acceptance session may be run against this build at any time, but the automated half of the case is not finished until the coordinator’s exact-head run binds them.

pendingHostedBindings.what: Every binding in this package that describes a head other than the candidate, listed by name. The gate DERIVES this set from the documents’ own `headSha` fields and refuses a difference in either direction, so a pending binding cannot go unlisted and a listed one cannot be decorative.
pendingHostedBindings.awaits: an exact-head CI run at the candidate 3c75f49a01e35b507461bf0929b0046e7140860a, taken by the phase coordinator
pendingHostedBindings.whyNoneCanBeTakenHere: A hosted figure is produced by a GitHub-hosted runner. This workstation can run the unit and web tiers and nothing else in this list: the backend and database tiers need a running PostgreSQL it does not host, the browser tier needs the full acceptance stack, and hosted CI, CodeQL, the dependency audit and the production build are properties of a RUN, not of a checkout.
pendingHostedBindings.whatTheCoordinatorMustDo: Run CI and bind the real figures. A binding leaves the pending state in exactly two ways and must declare which: (1) its `headSha` IS the candidate 3c75f49a01e35b507461bf0929b0046e7140860a; or (2) its `headSha` is a commit this repository CONTAINS, which DESCENDS from the candidate, whose apps/** and supabase/** the gate COMPUTES to be byte-identical to the candidate's, and which the binding marks `describesProductIdenticalSuccessor`. The second exists because the seal's own machinery cannot live inside the commit it seals, so hosted CI necessarily runs at a later head; under the old rule every hosted run forced another re-freeze whose seal commit moved the head again. What is still refused is a run at a head the candidate SUPERSEDES (that stays `describesSupersededHead`, and stays pending), a run at a head this repository does not contain, and a run at a descendant whose product differs — in which case the candidate must be re-frozen there and the local tiers re-measured, exactly as this cycle did.
